title: Absolute Residual Moment Identity
statement: Let $P$ be a finite product probability space with strictly positive coordinate weights, let $f$ take values in $\{-1,1\}$ at every point, and let $S$ be a set of coordinates. The expectation of the absolute residual from conditioning on $S$ equals the second moment of that residual: $\mathbb E_P|f-E_Sf|=\mathbb E_P(f-E_Sf)^2$.
hypotheses_covered: Finite product probability space with strictly positive coordinate weights
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $f:\Omega\to\{-1,1\}$, and $S\subseteq[n]$. For conditional expectation $E_S$ onto $S$, $\mathbb E_P|f-E_Sf|=\mathbb E_P(f-E_Sf)^2$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$.
